englishTranslation: Real dissipative free motion is distinguished from the ideal no-resistance model; not all free oscillations are said to die away quickly.
A periodic driving force alone is not said to guarantee a constant amplitude; net cycle energy balance and dissipation remain explicit.
Forced motion may coexist with free motion, and external work need not be positive at every instant.
Support, constraint, inertia, and dissipation qualifications remain, as does the cradle analogy's explicit non-caregiving disclaimer.
Small-angle and weak-resistance conditions remain. Constant-force equilibrium shifts, rhythmic energy input, build-up time, and structural amplitude limits remain.
Near-natural-frequency enhancement is conditional; equality alone does not guarantee maximum response, and resistance/driving conditions matter.
The apparatus, springs, ball, pulley rope, off-center disk pin, motor drive, supports, and unnumbered ruler match the frozen ZH concepts.
Transient decay and a finite steady amplitude are conditional on the stable damped model; settling need not be quick, and undamped countercases remain.
Steady frequency equality is restricted to a linear stable model with a single sinusoidal drive after transients. Natural frequency and transient frequencies remain distinct.

The disk rate relation retains constant rotation and a single identical drive cycle per revolution. Ordinary frequency is distinguished from angular frequency, and non-sinusoidal drives may produce harmonics.
